{{Citation needed|date=August 4, 2017}} {{Infobox Japan Law | Title = Prohibition of Tensha Shinto | Number = Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745 | Common Name = | Effective = | Type = {{ill|Administrative Procedure Act|ja|行政手続法}} | Contents = | Related = | Link = {{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}} |}}
'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).
This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮}}. Under this proclamation, {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}}—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.
== Contents == {{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符}} as they pass through {{ill|Shukuba|ja|宿場}}. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Haruaki|ja|土御門晴榮}}. All {{ill|Fuhanken sanchisei|ja|府藩県三治制}} must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)}}}}

'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan Edict|qq=}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9, 1870|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).

This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. Under this proclamation, [[:en:Onmyōji|Onmyōji]]—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.

== Contents ==
{{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Efu|qq=}} as they pass through [[:en:Shukuba|Shukuba]]. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruaki|qq=}}. All [[:en:Fuhanken sanchisei|Fuhanken sanchisei]] must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan|qq=|1=Dajōkan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125768223}}}}

'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan Edict|qq=}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9, 1870|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).

This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. Under this proclamation, [[:en:Onmyōji|Onmyōji]]—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.

== Contents ==
{{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Efu|qq=}} as they pass through [[:en:Shukuba|Shukuba]]. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruaki|qq=}}. All [[:en:Fuhanken sanchisei|Fuhanken sanchisei]] must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan|1=Dajōkan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125768223}}}}

'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan Edict|qq=}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9, 1870|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).
This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. Under this proclamation, [[:en:Onmyōji|Onmyōji]]—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.
== Contents == {{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Efu|qq=}} as they pass through [[:en:Shukuba|Shukuba]]. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruaki|qq=}}. All [[:en:Fuhanken sanchisei|Fuhanken sanchisei]] must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan|1=Dajōkan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125768223}}}}

'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan Edict|qq=}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9, 1870|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).

This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. Under this proclamation, [[:en:Onmyōji|Onmyōji]]—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.

== Contents ==
{{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Efu|qq=}} as they pass through [[:en:Shukuba|Shukuba]]. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruaki|qq=}}. All [[:en:Fuhanken sanchisei|Fuhanken sanchisei]] must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan|1=Dajōkan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125768223}}}}

'''Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17, Dajōkan Edict No. 745''' was a {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan Edict|qq=}} issued on {{ill|December 9, 1870|ja|1870th year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9, 1870|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Meiji 3 Intercalary October 17). It is also known as the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto''' (天社禁止令) or the '''Prohibition of Tensha Shinto Practices''' (天社神道禁止令).

This edict was issued as part of the Meiji government’s policy of abolishing the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. Under this proclamation, {{ill|Onmyōji|en|Onmyōji|WD=Q2274163|lt=Onmyōji|1=Onmyōji}}—recognized as an official profession—were officially banned from continuing their practice.

== Contents ==
{{Quotation|In the past, individuals calling themselves practitioners of {{ill|Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto|lt=Tensha Shinto|ja|天社土御門神道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and receiving licenses from the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家（安倍氏）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} have been found wearing swords and carrying {{ill|Efu|lt=Emblems|ja|会符|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Efu|qq=}} as they pass through {{ill|Shukuba|en|Shukuba|WD=Q1209783|lt=Shukuba|1=Shukuba}}. This practice is entirely unfounded, and henceforth these actions are prohibited and must be strictly enforced. Furthermore, the granting of any further licenses to disciples is entirely forbidden, as was recently ordered to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruaki|qq=}}. All {{ill|Fuhanken sanchisei|en|Fuhanken sanchisei|WD=Q11486110|lt=Fuhanken sanchisei|1=Fuhanken sanchisei}} must observe this decree and ensure the control of their jurisdictions accordingly.<ref>{{NDLDC|787950/259|Law Compilation, Meiji 3|format=EXTERNAL}}, Section 745, accessed August 4, 2017.</ref>|{{ill|Dajōkan|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dajōkan|1=Dajōkan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q125768223}}}}
